metaDescription: SecuEdge protects farm cooperatives, grain elevators and food producers from ransomware attacks timed to planting and harvest — and keeps food supply chains secure.

hero.headline: Harvest Season Shouldn't Be Ransomware Season
hero.sub: BlackMatter hit NEW Cooperative during harvest and demanded $5.9M. Crystal Valley Cooperative was struck the same week. JBS Foods paid $11M after a 2-month undetected breach shut all US beef plants. Agriculture is a target — SecuEdge closes the gaps attackers exploit.

challenges.title: Harvest-Timed Ransomware
challenges.desc: Attackers deliberately strike cooperatives and grain elevators during planting or harvest when operational disruption is maximally painful — grain cannot be sold, feed cannot be delivered, and payment pressure is extreme.

challenges.title: IoT and Smart Farming Devices on Flat Networks
challenges.desc: GPS-guided tractors, soil sensors, irrigation controllers and livestock monitors are increasingly IP-connected — and they typically share a flat network with cooperative management systems and back-office PCs.

challenges.title: Grain Co-op OT Systems with Minimal Security
challenges.desc: Grain elevator software, feed scheduling systems and grain transport logistics platforms are operational technology with no perimeter security, minimal patching and no network monitoring.

challenges.title: Remote Management Over Public Internet
challenges.desc: Farm sites, grain elevators and remote irrigation systems are managed remotely without VPN — SCADA-like control systems accessible directly over the internet, visible to anyone scanning agricultural IP ranges.

challenges.title: No Dedicated Security Staff
challenges.desc: Agriculture has the lowest cybersecurity spend per employee of any industry. Cooperatives have no security team, no incident response plan and no monitoring — breaches go undetected for months.

challenges.title: Food Supply Chain as Critical Infrastructure
challenges.desc: CISA designated food and agriculture as critical infrastructure after the JBS attack. The national security dimension means attackers know payments come faster when the food supply is at stake.

threats.title: Grain Management Systems Encrypted at Harvest
threats.desc: BlackMatter encrypted NEW Cooperative's grain transportation logistics and animal feed scheduling during peak Iowa harvest. Farmers could not sell grain, feed could not be delivered to livestock facilities — a direct food supply chain disruption.

threats.title: Multi-Month Undetected Dwell Time
threats.desc: REvil had 2 months of undetected access to JBS Foods before detonating ransomware across all 9 US meatpacking plants. No monitoring meant no detection until encryption was complete.

threats.title: Dual Simultaneous Attacks
threats.desc: NEW Cooperative and Crystal Valley Cooperative were both hit in the same week during harvest 2021 — demonstrating that ransomware groups coordinate attacks on agricultural targets during the highest-pressure period of the agricultural calendar.

threats.title: IoT Device as Network Entry Point
threats.desc: A compromised irrigation controller or GPS tractor module on a flat network provides a foothold into the same network as cooperative management systems, grain elevator controls and office workstations.

approach.title: Monitor for Long Dwell Time
approach.desc: JBS's 2-month undetected breach was possible because there was no network monitoring. SecuEdge logs all traffic — anomalous authentication attempts, new lateral connections between farm OT and cooperative IT, and bulk internal data access are visible in real time.

approach.title: Secure Remote Site Management via VPN
approach.desc: Every remote grain elevator, irrigation system and farm site connects via SecuEdge VPN tunnel — no internet-exposed management interfaces. Authenticated access replaces open public connectivity.

approach.title: Segment Operational Technology from Office IT
approach.desc: Grain elevator controls, feed scheduling systems and IoT farm devices sit in isolated VLANs with firewall rules preventing lateral movement to cooperative management and accounting systems.

approach.title: Block Ransomware C2 at DNS Layer
approach.desc: BlackMatter, REvil and DarkSide all require DNS callbacks to receive encryption keys. SecuEdge's malware and botnet DNS category blocking prevents this callback — ransomware stalls before it can encrypt.

capabilities.title: Network Monitoring & Long Dwell Detection
capabilities.desc: Continuous traffic logging surfaces the anomalous patterns — unusual authentication, new cross-segment connections, after-hours bulk file access — that characterise multi-month dwell periods before ransomware detonates.

capabilities.title: VPN for Remote Farm & Elevator Sites
capabilities.desc: Replace internet-exposed remote management of grain elevators, irrigation and livestock systems with SecuEdge VPN tunnels — authenticated, encrypted and monitored access from a single hardened gateway.

capabilities.title: Firewall OT/IT Segmentation
capabilities.desc: Separate VLANs for grain elevator OT, farm IoT devices, cooperative management systems and office IT — explicit firewall rules controlling all cross-zone communication.

capabilities.title: DNS & Content Category Blocking
capabilities.desc: Block BlackMatter, REvil and DarkSide C2 domains at the DNS layer across all cooperative and farm networks — production systems should never resolve uncategorised or newly-registered external domains.

capabilities.title: Load Balancing & WAN Failover
capabilities.desc: Dual-ISP failover keeps cooperative member transactions, grain sales and feed delivery communications live even when a primary link fails or is disrupted during an incident.

capabilities.title: Captive Portal for Seasonal Staff & Contractors
capabilities.desc: Seasonal harvest workers and equipment contractors connect via authenticated captive portal to an isolated network — no access to cooperative management systems or grain elevator controls.

process.title: Farm & Cooperative Network Audit
process.desc: Map all remote sites, internet-exposed management interfaces, IoT farm devices and grain elevator OT systems — identify flat network risks and unmonitored remote access paths.

process.title: Segment and Secure Before Planting/Harvest
process.desc: Deploy VPN for remote sites, implement OT/IT segmentation, configure DNS blocking and enable network monitoring — complete hardening before the next high-risk seasonal period.

process.title: Seasonal Readiness Reviews
process.desc: Review and tighten firewall rules before planting and harvest seasons, verify WAN failover, and brief cooperative staff on social engineering awareness before peak periods.

faqs.q: How would SecuEdge have changed the JBS Foods attack outcome?
faqs.a: REvil spent 2 months undetected on JBS's network. SecuEdge's real-time traffic monitoring would have surfaced anomalous east-west connections between plant systems and IT networks during that dwell period. DNS blocking would have prevented REvil's C2 callback. Network segmentation would have confined the blast radius to a single zone rather than all 9 plants.

faqs.q: Our co-op has grain elevators at five sites. How does SecuEdge protect all of them?
faqs.a: Each grain elevator site connects to cooperative HQ via SecuEdge site-to-site VPN. Elevator OT systems are in an isolated VLAN at each site. WAN failover at each site keeps member transactions live. All traffic flows through a central SecuEdge gateway where DNS blocking and monitoring applies to all sites simultaneously.

faqs.q: We have seasonal workers during harvest. How does SecuEdge handle temporary access?
faqs.a: SecuEdge's captive portal lets seasonal workers connect to WiFi via a branded splash page. Their devices land in an isolated VLAN with internet access and any permitted internal systems — access that's removed when the season ends by simply updating the firewall rules, with no per-device configuration needed.

faqs.q: We manage irrigation and GPS tractors remotely. Is that secure?
faqs.a: With SecuEdge VPN, remote management of irrigation and farm equipment happens over an authenticated, encrypted tunnel — not an open internet connection. The OT devices sit in a farm IoT VLAN isolated from cooperative management systems, so a compromised device cannot pivot to grain sales or member data.

cta.headline: Protect the Harvest Before Ransomware Does
cta.sub: Secure grain elevator OT, close remote access gaps and monitor for multi-month dwell time — so attackers can't time their strike to your most critical season.
